To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dorsolateral PFC is causally involved in the strategic control of selfish impulses and that the strategic control of these impulses is a necessary precondition for fair behaviour.

(1) strategic fairness is a norm that is acquired through socialization, (2) the right DLP FC plays a causal role in the control of self interest and (3) the DLP FC may have evolved to allow humans to strategically adapt their behavior and act fair if possible but selfishly if necessary.
the right DLP FC plays a causal role in the strategic acquisition and maintenance of fair behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how the DLPFC enables strategic fairness and thus contributes to the emergence of complex human society.
the question of why people are nice to others even when they could get away with being selfish.
the neurobiological basis of strategic fairness and the question whether the human brain is specialized for strategic fairness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our findings provide evidence for the role of the DLPFC in the strategic acquisition and control of fairness.
the right DLP FC is causally involved in the control and acquisition of strategic fairness.
the right DLPF plays a causal role in strategic fairness and that the strategic acquisition of fairness control is a human specific trait that evolved with the development of the human DLPFC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DLPFC enables the strategic control of selfish impulses and thus allows the emergence of social norms.
we show that the human right DLPFC is involved in the strategic control of selfish behaviour and that this strategic control is necessary for the existence of social norms.
the human DLPFC plays a causal role in the control of strategic fairness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
humans have the unique ability to control selfish behaviour strategically.
humans are able to strategically acquire the ability to act fairly.
the DLPFC may be involved in the acquisition of complex norm systems.
